      MCP Docs
      MCP Server Best Practices: Transport, Security and Tool Design

      MCP Server Best Practices: Transport, Security and Tool Design

      Before an MCP server faces real users or real data, settle the deployment shape, transport, and auth model; meet the MUST rules for Streamable HTTP and OAuth; and make sure tool definitions let a model correct itself. Each practice points to the official text that requires it, with failure modes and recovery steps; a script in the text tests the HTTP rules of a live endpoint.

      Scope. Server side only, 2026-07-28 revision. Client behavior is covered by the official client best practices; hardening a local stdio server on a developer machine is covered by Local MCP Server Security.

      1. Pick the deployment shape first

      Most security decisions follow from where the server runs and who can reach it. Decide this before writing handlers.

      Your situationUseAuthenticationOfficial basis
      A tool for one user, started by the host on the same machinestdioRead credentials from the environment. Do not implement the HTTP authorization flowAuthorization is OPTIONAL; implementations on stdio SHOULD NOT follow the HTTP authorization spec (Basic protocol: Auth)
      A local HTTP server that other processes on the machine could reachStreamable HTTPBind to 127.0.0.1, validate Origin, and require a token or use IPC with restricted accessStreamable HTTP, “Security & Endpoint”; Security Best Practices, “Local MCP Server Compromise”
      A shared server for many usersStreamable HTTPOAuth 2.1 resource server: Protected Resource Metadata, token validation, audience bindingAuthorization
      A server that calls another API on the user’s behalfStreamable HTTPA token issued for your server. Use separate credentials downstream and never forward the client’s tokenAuthorization, “Token Handling”: servers MUST NOT accept or transit tokens issued for other resources

      2. Make the server stateless on purpose

      Revision 2026-07-28 has no protocol sessions. Every request carries its own _meta (protocol version, client info, capabilities), and servers MUST NOT rely on earlier requests on the same connection (Basic protocol: Statelessness). A client may interleave unrelated work on one connection, so a connection or process is not a conversation.

      State that spans requests, such as a cart, a draft or a long job, lives behind an explicit handle that the model carries as an ordinary tool argument (Tools: Stateful Tools, non-normative).

      You need to rememberDoAvoid
      A cart, a transaction, a long-running jobReturn an opaque handle from a creation tool and accept it as an argument on later callsKeying state on the connection, the process, or an Mcp-Session-Id header
      Who may use a handleStore state under <user_id>:<handle> where the user comes from the verified token, and reject other principalsTreating possession of a handle as authentication
      Handle formatCryptographically random, opaque, expiringCounters, timestamps, or identifiers that encode internal structure
      ExpiryState the retention rule in the creation tool’s description, and answer an expired handle with a tool execution error that says soSilent failure or a generic protocol error
      Scaling outKeep shared state in a store behind the handle so any instance can serve any requestRequiring the same connection or process for related requests (SHOULD NOT)

      A server that supports only this revision should ignore an incoming Mcp-Session-Id and neither mint nor echo one (Streamable HTTP: Earlier Streamable HTTP Revisions).

      3. The rules a remote server must pass

      Each row is a practice, the level of the official text behind it, where to read it, and which probe check in section 6 exercises it. “Guidance” marks text that describes behavior without an RFC 2119 keyword.

      #PracticeLevelOfficial sourceProbe check
      1Implement server/discover and list the versions you support in supportedVersionsMUSTDiscoverydiscover
      2Validate Origin on all incoming connections. If it is present and invalid, answer 403 ForbiddenMUSTStreamable HTTP, “Security & Endpoint”origin
      3Reject a request whose Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name or MCP-Protocol-Version header is missing, malformed or different from the body: 400 with JSON-RPC error -32020 (HeaderMismatch)MUSTStreamable HTTP, “Server Validation”method-header-missing, method-header-mismatch
      4For an unsupported protocol version answer 400 with UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (-32022) and list the supported versionsMUSTStreamable HTTP, “Protocol Version Header”unsupported-version, unsupported-version-lists-supported
      5For an unknown RPC method answer 404 with -32601MUSTStreamable HTTP, “Protocol Version Header”unknown-method
      6Reject a request without MCP-Protocol-Version, unless you deliberately serve clients older than 2025-06-18MUST, for servers that do not support such clientsStreamable HTTP, “Protocol Version Header”version-header-missing (WARN)
      7Answer GET and DELETE on the endpoint with 405; ignore Mcp-Session-Id and do not mint session IDsSHOULDStreamable HTTP, “Earlier Streamable HTTP Revisions”get-not-allowed, no-session-id (WARN)
      8Validate all tool inputs, enforce access control, rate limit invocations, sanitize outputsMUSTTools, “Security Considerations”not probed
      9Report input validation failures as results with isError: true; report an unknown tool as a protocol error (-32602)GuidanceTools, “Error Handling”tool-input-error, unknown-tool (WARN)
      10Serve Protected Resource Metadata with at least one entry in authorization_servers, and advertise it through the resource_metadata parameter of WWW-Authenticate or a well-known URIMUSTAuthorization Server Discoveryauth-resource-metadata
      11Validate access tokens, accept only tokens issued for this server as audience, answer invalid or expired tokens with 401MUSTAuthorization, “Token Handling”auth-required, auth-invalid-token, auth-audience
      12Never accept or pass through tokens issued for another resourceMUST NOTAuthorization, “Token Handling”; Security Best Practices, “Token Passthrough”auth-audience (acceptance only)
      13For insufficient scope answer 403 with WWW-Authenticate carrying error="insufficient_scope", scope and resource_metadata, and put every scope the operation needs into one challengeSHOULDAuthorization, “Scope Challenge Handling”not probed
      14Use least-privilege scopes: a small initial set, no wildcard scopes, no full catalog in scopes_supportedGuidanceSecurity Best Practices, “Scope Minimization”not probed
      15Make state handles unpredictable and bind them server-side to the authenticated userSHOULDSecurity Best Practices, “State Handle Hijacking”not probed

      Rows 8, 13, 14 and 15 need your application logic or a token with limited scope, so no generic probe can cover them. Write those tests yourself. The scenarios are in section 5.

      4. Define tools so the model can recover

      RuleLevelOfficial source
      Name: 1 to 128 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - ., case-sensitive, unique within the serverSHOULDTools, “Tool Names”
      inputSchema is a valid JSON Schema object, never null. For a tool without parameters use { "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false }MUST (valid object); recommended formTools, “Tool”
      If you declare outputSchema, every structured result conforms to it. Also return the serialized JSON in a text block for older clientsMUST; SHOULDTools, “Output Schema” and “Structured Content”
      tools/list returns the tools available to the requesting client and does not vary per connection or as a side effect of other requests. It MAY vary with the authorization on the request. Keep the order deterministicMUST NOT vary per connection; SHOULD for orderTools, “Capabilities”
      Return validation and business-rule failures as isError: true results with a message that says what was wrong and what is valid, such as the format or range. Clients SHOULD show execution errors to the model, while protocol errors are less likely to be recoveredGuidanceTools, “Error Handling”
      Do not mark secrets or personal data with x-mcp-header; header values are visible to network intermediariesSHOULD NOTTools, “x-mcp-header”
      Do not depend on annotations as a security control. Clients MUST treat them as untrusted unless the server is trustedMUST (client)Tools, “Tool”

      Guidance that does not belong in a single tool description, such as how tools relate to each other, goes into the server instructions. Server Instructions in Practice covers where that field is delivered in each revision and how to test it.

      5. Failure modes and recovery

      SymptomLikely causeHow to confirmFix
      Every request through a gateway fails with 400 and -32020A proxy drops or rewrites Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name or MCP-Protocol-Version. The spec counts a missing or mismatched header as a validation failureRun the probe against the origin and through the gateway, then compare method-header-*Forward the three headers unchanged and keep body and headers in sync
      A client retries after -32022 and never succeedsIt ignores data.supported, or your list holds versions it does not speakRead data.supported and data.requested in the error bodyReturn an accurate list. The client retries with a version both sides support (Versioning)
      A legacy client fails on its first requestA modern-only server and a client that starts with initialize. SDK 2.3.0 answered a request without MCP-Protocol-Version with 400 and -32600version-header-missingAccept that, or implement the earlier-revision behavior described in the corresponding spec revision
      A browser app gets 403The Origin allow-list lacks the app’s originRepeat the request with the app’s OriginAdd exact origins. The probe only sends a hostile origin, so add a test for each allowed one
      Every call returns 401 after enabling authThe token was minted for another audience, or the server compares against a resource identifier that differs from what the client requestedRun the probe with --token; discover must pass firstBind tokens to the server’s canonical URI and configure the same URI in the server
      A token issued for another service is acceptedNothing checks the audience. In SDK 2.3.0, AuthSettings.validate_token_resource is unset by default: the SDK warns, does not check, and says it will default to True in 3.0auth-audience fails with got 200 (reproduced in section 6)Set validate_token_resource=True, or check the audience inside your TokenVerifier
      The client keeps sending the user through consentThe server challenges one scope at a timeCount the 403 challenges for one operationPut all scopes the operation needs into one challenge; clients should cap retries
      One user reaches another user’s cartA guessable handle, or a handle not bound to the callerReplay a handle with a second user’s tokenRandom opaque handles, keyed by <user_id>:<handle> with the user taken from the verified token
      The model repeats the same bad callThe failure came back as a protocol error or as vague textCompare a JSON-RPC error with an isError result and read the messageReturn isError: true naming the field and the valid values
      The tool list differs between two connectionsThe listing depends on connection state or on unordered storageCall tools/list on two connections and diffCompute it from the request’s authorization alone and sort it

      Test scenarios to add to your own CI for the rows the probe cannot cover: a token with too few scopes gets 403 and the challenge lists every needed scope; a second user’s token cannot use the first user’s handle; an expired handle returns an isError result; two connections get the same tools/list for the same token; a tool call over the rate limit is refused.

      6. Run the HTTP probe

      probe_http.py uses only the Python standard library. It sends the requests behind the probed rows of section 3 and prints one line per check. FAIL means a MUST is not met, WARN means a SHOULD or the tools page’s error guidance is not followed. Exit code 0 means no FAIL, 1 at least one FAIL, 2 means the endpoint was unreachable.

      python3 probe_http.py http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp --tool echo --bad-args '{"text":123}'
python3 probe_http.py http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp --tool echo --bad-args '{"text":123}' \
  --token good-token --expect-auth --bad-audience-token other-audience-token
      probe_http.py
      #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Probe a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint against the HTTP rules of spec 2026-07-28 (stdlib only).

Usage: probe_http.py URL [--tool NAME --bad-args JSON] [--token T [--expect-auth] [--bad-audience-token T]]
Levels: FAIL = a MUST in the spec is not met, WARN = a SHOULD or the tools page's error guidance is not followed
(version-header-missing is WARN because a server may serve pre-2025-06-18 clients and treat the request as 2025-03-26).
Exit code: 0 no FAIL, 1 at least one FAIL, 2 endpoint unreachable.
"""
import argparse
import http.client
import json
import sys
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

VERSION = "2026-07-28"
EVIL_ORIGIN = "https://evil.example"
counts = {"PASS": 0, "WARN": 0, "FAIL": 0}


def meta(version):
    return {
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": version,
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo": {"name": "probe", "version": "0"},
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": {},
    }


def parse(raw):
    """Return the JSON-RPC response from a JSON body or an SSE stream, else None."""
    try:
        return json.loads(raw)
    except ValueError:
        pass
    found = None
    for line in raw.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("data:"):
            try:
                msg = json.loads(line[5:].strip())
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if isinstance(msg, dict) and ("result" in msg or "error" in msg):
                found = msg
    return found


def request(url, verb="POST", method=None, params=None, headers=None, version=VERSION):
    """Send one request; a header whose value is None is removed. Returns (status, headers, body)."""
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    cls = http.client.HTTPSConnection if parts.scheme == "https" else http.client.HTTPConnection
    conn = cls(parts.netloc, timeout=10)
    hdrs = {"Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream", "MCP-Protocol-Version": version}
    payload = None
    if verb == "POST":
        hdrs.update({"Content-Type": "application/json", "Mcp-Method": method})
        if params and "name" in params:
            hdrs["Mcp-Name"] = params["name"]
        payload = json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": method,
                              "params": {**(params or {}), "_meta": meta(version)}})
    hdrs.update(headers or {})
    conn.request(verb, parts.path or "/", payload, {k: v for k, v in hdrs.items() if v is not None})
    resp = conn.getresponse()
    raw = resp.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    conn.close()
    return resp.status, resp, parse(raw)


def code(body):
    err = body.get("error") if isinstance(body, dict) else None
    return err.get("code") if isinstance(err, dict) else None


def show(status, rpc_code):
    return "%s/%s" % (status, rpc_code) if rpc_code is not None else str(status)


def report(name, ok, detail, level="FAIL"):
    status = "PASS" if ok else level
    counts[status] += 1
    print("%s %s: %s" % (status, name, detail))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("url")
    ap.add_argument("--tool", help="name of an existing tool, enables the tool-error check")
    ap.add_argument("--bad-args", default="{}", help="JSON arguments that violate the tool's input schema")
    ap.add_argument("--token", help="bearer token that the server accepts")
    ap.add_argument("--expect-auth", action="store_true", help="the endpoint is protected: run the auth checks")
    ap.add_argument("--bad-audience-token", help="a valid token issued for a different resource")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.expect_auth and not args.token:
        ap.error("--expect-auth needs --token (the other checks must get past authentication)")
    auth = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + args.token} if args.token else {}
    url = args.url

    try:
        status, _, body = request(url, method="server/discover", headers=auth)
    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as exc:
        print("ERROR endpoint unreachable: %s" % exc)
        return 2
    result = body.get("result") if isinstance(body, dict) else None
    ok = status == 200 and isinstance(result, dict) and VERSION in result.get("supportedVersions", [])
    report("discover", ok, "HTTP %s, supportedVersions %s" % (status, (result or {}).get("supportedVersions")))
    tools = "tools" in (result or {}).get("capabilities", {})

    def expect(name, want_status, want_code, **kw):
        st, _, b = request(url, **{"headers": auth, **kw})
        report(name, st == want_status and (want_code is None or code(b) == want_code),
               "want %s, got %s" % (show(want_status, want_code), show(st, code(b))))
        return b

    expect("origin", 403, None, method="server/discover", headers={**auth, "Origin": EVIL_ORIGIN})
    expect("method-header-missing", 400, -32020, method="server/discover", headers={**auth, "Mcp-Method": None})
    expect("method-header-mismatch", 400, -32020, method="server/discover", headers={**auth, "Mcp-Method": "tools/list"})
    b = expect("unsupported-version", 400, -32022, method="server/discover", version="2099-01-01",
               headers={**auth})
    supported = ((b or {}).get("error") or {}).get("data", {}).get("supported") if isinstance(b, dict) else None
    report("unsupported-version-lists-supported", bool(supported) and VERSION in supported, "data.supported = %s" % supported)
    expect("unknown-method", 404, -32601, method="nope/nothing")

    st, _, b = request(url, method="server/discover", headers={**auth, "MCP-Protocol-Version": None})
    report("version-header-missing", st == 400, "want 400, got %s" % show(st, code(b)), "WARN")
    st, _, _ = request(url, verb="GET", headers=auth)
    report("get-not-allowed", st == 405, "want 405, got %s" % st, "WARN")
    st, resp, _ = request(url, method="server/discover", headers={**auth, "Mcp-Session-Id": "probe-session"})
    report("no-session-id", resp.getheader("Mcp-Session-Id") is None, "Mcp-Session-Id in response: %s" % resp.getheader("Mcp-Session-Id"), "WARN")

    if args.tool:
        st, _, b = request(url, method="tools/call", params={"name": args.tool, "arguments": json.loads(args.bad_args)}, headers=auth)
        is_error = isinstance(b, dict) and (b.get("result") or {}).get("isError") is True
        report("tool-input-error", st == 200 and is_error, "want 200 with result.isError=true, got %s" % show(st, "isError" if is_error else code(b)), "WARN")
        st, _, b = request(url, method="tools/call", params={"name": "no_such_tool", "arguments": {}}, headers=auth)
        report("unknown-tool", code(b) == -32602, "want JSON-RPC error -32602, got %s" % show(st, code(b) or "result"), "WARN")
    elif tools:
        print("SKIP tool checks: pass --tool NAME --bad-args JSON")

    if args.expect_auth:
        st, resp, b = request(url, method="server/discover")
        challenge = resp.getheader("WWW-Authenticate") or ""
        report("auth-required", st == 401, "no token: want 401, got %s" % st)
        report("auth-invalid-token", request(url, method="server/discover", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer invalid"})[0] == 401,
               "garbage token must get 401")
        if args.bad_audience_token:
            st = request(url, method="server/discover", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + args.bad_audience_token})[0]
            report("auth-audience", st == 401, "token for another resource: want 401, got %s" % st)
        meta_url = challenge.split('resource_metadata="')[1].split('"')[0] if 'resource_metadata="' in challenge else None
        origin = "%s://%s" % (urlsplit(url).scheme, urlsplit(url).netloc)
        well_known = "/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"
        found = None
        for candidate in [meta_url, origin + well_known + urlsplit(url).path, origin + well_known]:
            if not candidate:
                continue
            st, _, doc = request(candidate, verb="GET", headers={})
            if st == 200 and isinstance(doc, dict):
                found = doc
                break
        report("auth-resource-metadata", bool(found and found.get("authorization_servers")),
               "challenge resource_metadata=%s; document authorization_servers=%s" % (meta_url, (found or {}).get("authorization_servers")))

    print("%d pass, %d warn, %d fail" % (counts["PASS"], counts["WARN"], counts["FAIL"]))
    return 1 if counts["FAIL"] else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        sys.exit(main())
    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as exc:
        print("ERROR connection failed: %s" % exc)
        sys.exit(2)

      The two reference servers use the official Python SDK (pip install mcp==2.3.0):

      ref_server.py
      """Official Python SDK (mcp==2.3.0) server on Streamable HTTP, http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp, no auth."""
from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer

server = MCPServer("ref")


@server.tool()
def echo(text: str) -> str:
    """Echo text."""
    return text


if __name__ == "__main__":
    server.run("streamable-http")
      auth_ref_server.py
      """Same server behind bearer-token auth, http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp.

Tokens: good-token is issued for this server; other-audience-token is valid but issued for another resource.
"""
from mcp.server.auth.provider import AccessToken
from mcp.server.auth.settings import AuthSettings
from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer

RESOURCE = "http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp"


class Verifier:
    async def verify_token(self, token: str) -> AccessToken | None:
        if token == "good-token":
            return AccessToken(token=token, client_id="probe", scopes=[], resource=RESOURCE)
        if token == "other-audience-token":
            return AccessToken(token=token, client_id="probe", scopes=[], resource="https://other.example/mcp")
        return None


server = MCPServer(
    "ref-auth",
    token_verifier=Verifier(),
    auth=AuthSettings(
        issuer_url="https://auth.example.com",
        resource_server_url=RESOURCE,
        validate_token_resource=True,
    ),
)


@server.tool()
def echo(text: str) -> str:
    """Echo text."""
    return text


if __name__ == "__main__":
    server.run("streamable-http", port=8001)

      What the probe reported on this setup (Python 3.14, macOS, mcp==2.3.0):

      TargetResult
      SDK server without auth (ref_server.py)11 pass, 1 warn, 0 fail

      A stub written from the spec text, without and with auth12 pass, 0 warn, 0 fail; 16 pass, 0 warn, 0 fail
      The stub with one rule broken at a time, 11 variants8 variants fail the named check, 3 variants only warn, none passes silently

      PASS discover: HTTP 200, supportedVersions ['2026-07-28']

PASS method-header-missing: want 400/-32020, got 400/-32020
PASS method-header-mismatch: want 400/-32020, got 400/-32020

PASS tool-input-error: want 200 with result.isError=true, got 200/isError

PASS auth-audience: token for another resource: want 401, got 401
PASS auth-resource-metadata: challenge resource_metadata=http://127.0.0.1:8001/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp; document authorization_servers=['https://auth.example.com']
15 pass, 1 warn, 0 fail

      How to read it:

      • The one warning is a finding, not a bug in the probe. The tools page lists “Unknown tool” under protocol errors with -32602. SDK 2.3.0 returns a normal result with isError: true instead. The text is guidance rather than a MUST, and the model can recover from either, but pick one behavior on purpose and test it.
      • The default-audience run shows why negative tests matter. The server answered 200 for a token issued for https://other.example/mcp. Nothing crashed and the happy path worked, so only a negative test finds it.
      • Passing proves the listed behaviors on one setup. The probe does not test: that an allow-listed origin passes, TLS, rate limits, scope challenges, streamed (SSE) responses, cancellation, x-mcp-header mirroring, multi round-trip requests, output sanitization, or load. A stub and the SDK passing the same checks are two independent readings of the spec, but they do not rule out a shared misreading, so keep the matrix in section 3 as the review list.

      7. Before you ship

      • You chose the deployment shape in section 1 and wrote down why.
      • Nothing depends on connection or process identity; every handle is opaque, expiring and bound to its owner.
      • Origin validation, header validation and version errors pass the probe, and your gateway forwards the three mirrored headers.
      • For a protected server: invalid, expired and wrong-audience tokens get 401; the metadata document names an authorization server; no token is forwarded downstream.
      • Tool names, schemas and result shapes follow section 4, and validation failures are isError results the model can act on.
      • Rows 8, 13, 14 and 15 have tests in your own suite.
      • You re-run the probe when you change the SDK, the gateway or the authorization server.

      Versions and Verification

      Spec facts come from the 2026-07-28 pages published on this site. The experiments in section 6 ran locally against the official Python SDK 2.3.0 and are labeled as such.
